title: Sociological perspectives
examples: How does each perspective see the role of the family?
Can you compare how Marxism and functionalism view social change?
What is the main difference between feminist and interactionist views?

explain.say: Today we explore different ways to see society. We will look at four main perspectives. These help us understand social life better.
Functionalism sees society as a body with parts. Each part has a job to keep the whole system stable. Like organs working together in the body.
Marxism focuses on class struggle and economic power. It argues that conflict between classes drives history forward. Money and ownership are key here.
Feminism examines how gender shapes society and power. It highlights how patriarchal structures limit women's potential. Gender roles are central to this view.
Interactionism looks at small daily interactions. It suggests meaning is created through face-to-face contact. We act based on how we interpret others.

In real life, think about a school uniform policy. Functionalism sees it promoting unity. Marxism might see it hiding class differences. Feminism might question its gender implications. Interactionism notes how students negotiate the rules.

items: Interactionism | How students use the uniform daily

faq.q: How do I know which perspective to use for a question?
faq.a: Think about what the question emphasizes. If it is about stability, functionalism is useful. If it is about money, Marxism might fit best.
asks: Which theory is best for social problems?
When should I use functionalism versus Marxism?

faq.q: Does one perspective always contradict another?
faq.a: Not always, but they often focus on different levels. Functionalism looks at the whole system, while interactionism looks at small moments.
asks: Are these theories always in opposition?

faq.q: What is the main focus of feminism in sociology?
faq.a: Feminism primarily analyzes how gender inequality is built into social structures. It challenges male dominance in many areas of life.
asks: What does feminism critique about society?
Is feminism only about women's rights?

faq.q: Can we use all four perspectives at once?
faq.a: Yes, strong essays often compare them. You can show how each perspective offers a unique lens on the same issue.
asks: Is comparison always the best way to answer?
Should I use multiple theories together?

faq.q: What is the difference between class struggle and gender struggle?
faq.a: Class struggle focuses on economic ownership and wealth distribution. Gender struggle focuses on power imbalances related to gender roles.
asks: Is Marxism only about rich and poor?
Does feminism only talk about men and women?

facts: Functionalism views society as a complex system whose parts work together.
Marxism argues that the economic base determines the social superstructure.
Feminism critiques patriarchal structures that maintain gender inequality.
Interactionism emphasizes the subjective meaning people attach to symbols.

quiz.say: A sociologist studies how people interpret a handshake as a greeting. Which perspective is most relevant?
quiz.why: Interactionism focuses specifically on the meaning created during face-to-face interactions.

wrong.0: Functionalism would focus on the handshake's role in maintaining social order, not the meaning itself.
wrong.1: Marxism would ignore the gesture and focus only on who has the power in the exchange.
wrong.2: Feminism would analyze if the greeting was gendered, missing the general interaction point.

quiz.say: If a sociologist argues that the law exists mainly to maintain social stability, they are likely using which perspective?
quiz.why: Functionalism views institutions like law as necessary parts maintaining the whole system's stability.

wrong.1: Marxism would argue the law mainly serves the interests of the ruling economic class.
wrong.2: Feminism would question whose interests the law actually protects regarding gender.
wrong.3: Interactionism would look at how people actually follow or break the law in daily life.

quiz.say: Which perspective would most likely analyze the division of unpaid domestic labour between genders?
quiz.why: Feminism specifically examines how gender roles dictate unpaid labour and power imbalances.

wrong.0: Interactionism would focus on the specific arguments used within the household about the labour division.
wrong.2: Functionalism might see this division as a necessary, stable role for society.
wrong.3: Marxism might view it as unpaid labour that supports the capitalist system, but feminism is more specific to gender.
